Flag iSNV sites based on quality criteria

Source: R/AllGenerics.R, R/qc-filters.R
flagISNV.Rd

Generic for applying quality control filters to within-host variant data. The default method operates on WithinHostExperiment objects. Other packages can define methods for alternative containers.

Applies quality control filters to a WithinHostExperiment. Instead of removing variants, this function sets the corresponding entries in the qcPass assay to FALSE. Each filtering step is recorded in the qcLog for full reproducibility.

Usage

flagISNV(x, filter = ISNVFilter(), ...)

# S4 method for class 'WithinHostExperiment'
flagISNV(x, filter = ISNVFilter(), ...)

Arguments

x

A WithinHostExperiment object.

filter

An ISNVFilter object (default: ISNVFilter()).

...

Must be empty. Any further argument is an error, so that a misspelled argument name cannot be silently ignored.

Value

The filtered object (same class as input).

A WithinHostExperiment with updated qcPass assay and qcLog.

Details

Filtering steps are applied in order:

  1. Minimum read depth (minDepth)

  2. Minimum alternative allele frequency (minFreq)

  3. Maximum alternative allele frequency (maxFreq)

  4. Minimum alternative allele read count (minAltReads)

  5. Strand bias (maxStrandBias) – only if fwdAltCount and revAltCount assays exist

  6. Replicate concordance (replicateConc) – only if the filter holds a ConcordanceRule

The filter is checked with validObject() first, so a threshold or a rule changed with @<- into one its class refuses is an error rather than a step applied.

Base and mapping quality are not filtered here: the object holds no per-site quality, so those thresholds belong in the variant caller.

The replicate step compares every pair of samples that share a value of the replicate_group column of colData and flags a site that fails the rule in every sample of the group. It compares the calls as made, before the thresholds above, so it flags what flagReplicateDiscordance flags with the same settings, and it records the same two qcLog rows. A rule with no replicate_group column, or with no group of two or more samples, is an error rather than a step that checks nothing. Samples outside any such group are named in a warning and are filtered by the other thresholds only.

See also

ISNVFilter for filter configuration, ConcordanceRule for the replicate rule, passedISNV for extracting passed variants, qcSummary for QC report, flagReplicateDiscordance for replicate QC.

Examples

vcf <- system.file("extdata", "test_donor.vcf",
    package = "WithinHostExperiment")
whe <- readWithinHost(vcf,
    colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(sample_id = "donor"),
    caller = "ivar")
whe <- flagISNV(whe, ISNVFilter(minDepth = 500L))
qcLog(whe)
#> DataFrame with 4 rows and 6 columns
#>               step   parameter       value n_flagged  n_passed
#>        <character> <character> <character> <integer> <integer>
#> 1     depth_filter    minDepth         500         1        14
#> 2  min_freq_filter     minFreq        0.03         0        14
#> 3  max_freq_filter     maxFreq         0.5         0        14
#> 4 alt_reads_filter minAltReads          10         0        14
#>             timestamp
#>           <character>
#> 1 2026-11-26T15:37:52
#> 2 2026-11-26T15:37:52
#> 3 2026-11-26T15:37:52
#> 4 2026-11-26T15:37:52
passedISNV(whe)
#> WithinHostExperiment with 14 variant sites and 1 samples
#>   assays(5): altFreq, totalDepth, refCount, altCount, qcPass
#>   qcLog: 4 filtering step(s)
#>   transmission pairs: 0
